evidence: frontend/apps/ppt-web/src/routes/groups/ai-dashboards.tsx:48 and :81 — both AI-dashboard routes invoke acknowledge mutations as fire-and-forget `onAcknowledge={(id) => acknowledge.mutate(id)}` / `onAcknowledgePrediction={(id) => acknowledge.mutate(id)}` with NO second-arg onError and NO try/catch (these are sync `.mutate`, not awaited `.mutateAsync`). The route forwards only the loading state down to the page component — `pendingAcknowledgeId={pendingAcknowledgeId}` (ai-dashboards.tsx:46, :79, derived from `acknowledge.isPending`) — but it never forwards `acknowledge.isError` or `acknowledge.error`, so the child pages (SentimentDashboardPage / PredictiveMaintenancePage) have no prop through which to render a failure. The backing hooks seal the gap shut: useAcknowledgeSentimentAlert (features/sentiment/hooks/useSentiment.ts:89-102) and useAcknowledgeMaintenancePrediction (features/predictive-maintenance/hooks/usePredictiveMaintenance.ts:72-86) each define ONLY `mutationFn` + `onSuccess` (cache invalidation) with NO onError. Net effect on a failed POST `/alerts/{id}/acknowledge` or `/predictions/{id}/acknowledge` (401/403/409/5xx): the cache is NOT invalidated (onSuccess skipped), the pending spinner clears, and the user sees the alert/prediction silently remain un-acknowledged with zero feedback — a classic swallowed-error user-facing path. Contrast with the well-handled siblings in the SAME segment that DO surface errors: SessionsPage (features/settings/pages/SessionsPage.tsx) renders `revokeSession.isError`/`revokeAllOthers.isError` role=alert blocks; financial.tsx (routes/groups/financial.tsx:179,:206,:308,:326) and rentals.tsx (routes/groups/rentals.tsx) attach explicit onError toasts/handleRentalsMutationError on every mutation. This is an unhandled error on a user-facing mutation path -> severity MEDIUM (+2). Suggested cloud-landable fix (frontend-only, vitest-verifiable): add `onError` to each acknowledge hook (surface via the shared errorHandler/toast used elsewhere), or forward `acknowledge.isError`/`acknowledge.error` from ai-dashboards.tsx down to the page components and render an alert, mirroring SessionsPage. Reachability traced statically (route -> hook -> consumer render); failure frequency not observable statically, hence confidence medium.

frontend/apps/ppt-web/src/lib/websocket.ts:94-101 — buildWebSocketUrl(base, token) places the raw JWT access token into a query-string parameter: `url.searchParams.set('token', token); return url.toString();`, and the socket is opened with it at websocket.ts:369 `new WebSocket(buildWebSocketUrl(this.url, token), ['ppt.v1'])`, where `token = this.getToken()` (websocket.ts:330) is wired to the live access token via contexts/WebSocketContext.tsx:261 `getToken: () => authRef.current.accessToken`. Passing a bearer credential in a URL (even over wss://, which encrypts it on the wire) is a well-known sensitive-data-in-URL exposure (OWASP): the `?token=<jwt>` is captured in plaintext by any server/reverse-proxy/load-balancer access log, APM/observability spans that record request URLs, and — for the WS upgrade request — potentially intermediary diagnostics, where it then sits at rest readable by anyone with log access for the token's full TTL. The code comments (websocket.ts:86-92, :186-193) show this mirrors the api-server contract (server reads JWT from the `token` query param), so it is a deliberate but under-mitigated design: the token is not short-circuited to a single-use/ticket token, and browsers' inability to set custom headers on the native WebSocket handshake is the usual justification — but the standard safer pattern is a short-lived one-time WS ticket exchanged over an authenticated HTTP call, then presented in the query param, so a leaked log entry is useless after first use. Severity MEDIUM (+2): a real credential-exposure class on the WS auth path, bounded by access-token TTL and log access, not a direct auth bypass. Suggested vector (cross-stack, backend + ppt-web): introduce a short-lived single-use WS ticket endpoint and have buildWebSocketUrl carry the ticket instead of the full access JWT; at minimum, scrub `token` from access-log URL capture at the proxy. Reachability traced statically (WebSocketContext.getToken -> connect -> buildWebSocketUrl -> new WebSocket); confidence medium (static; depends on deployment log configuration which is not observable in-repo).
